findings.pdf_says: GENERAL FORMAT FOR COMMUNICATION DESCRIPTION ENTRY
findings.why_it_matters: The centred, underlined general-format title that heads Format 2 and Format 3 of the CD entry is transcribed as a plain underlined paragraph, not a heading. The identical title on page 207, and every other general-format title in this batch (pages 205, 206, 209-216), is a '## ' heading, so this page's CD formats drop out of the document outline and heading-based slicing.

findings.pdf_says: SW CLOSE { file-name-1 [ {REEL | UNIT} [FOR REMOVAL] | WITH {NO REWIND | LOCK} ] } ...  (one left brace before file-name-1, drawn as a single brace spanning the bracket, with CLOSE to its left)
findings.why_it_matters: The drawn SW CLOSE format is misaligned: the middle row 'SW        <u>CLOSE</u> ┤ file-name-1   │ ... │ ├ …' is shifted about nine columns right of the other six rows. In the rendered figure the outer brace (column of ╭ ┤ │ ┤ ╰) stands to the RIGHT of where CLOSE prints, the bracket's left edge (┌/└ at the column of file-name-1) cuts through 'file-name-1', and its right edge and closing brace on that row sit beyond the ┐/╮ of the rows above. The outer brace also carries three ┤ middle marks. The geometry no longer shows that file-name-1 and the optional REEL/UNIT-or-WITH bracket are inside one repeated brace; the intended syntax is recoverable only by reading the glyphs in order.
